Q1. Create a class student having data members as name (string) and rollno (int). Each student can be either a cricketer or footballer or both. Every cricketer has runs (int) and wickets (int) while every footballer has goals scored (int) and assists (int). A star performer is a student who plays both cricket and football have a star performer index calculated using the following formula: star performer index = [(runs-1000)/runs+(goal-10)/goal]. Develop a C++ program that can simulate the following rules adhering to the above inheritance structure (you can define additional necessary method).
a) Create a star performer object.
b) Set the student details and the cricketer/footballer or both by calling the appropriate methods from the star performer class.
c) Compute the star performer index value using the above mentioned formula.
d) Display the details of the students if he/she is a star performer. A Student is considered as a star performer if and only if star performer index is grater then zero.
[CO2(Applying), 5M]

Q2. Draw a UML class diagram for a restaurant, which has its name, location, owner name. Restaurant has traditional south Indian menu which is having dishes (items) details and prices, some are available all day and some are specifically available in breakfast and evening. Whenever customer with name, location and contact number, places any order, it contains the items from the menu and also their quantity and bill (total amount to pay). After the payment, the receipt is generated for the order having all food details and customer details. The restaurant has two types of staff members, chef staff for cooking and other operational staff for taking order and delivering it. A feedback is also taken from the customer after delivering his order. Show the complete diagram with appropriate relations with class details, types of relationship and its multiplicity.
[CO5(Creating), 5M]

Q3. An International ship can be classified as either a Cruise ship or Cargo carrier. Each ship has a name (String), fuel capacity (int), valuation (double), owning company (string) and insurance premium (double). A cruise ship has additional features like number of passenger (int), number of pools (int), food storage (double) while a cargo carrier has number of crews (int), number of risky zones (int) and inflammable material quantity (double). The insurance premium for each type of ship is computed using following formula.

For cruise ship: insurance premium = (valuation + fuel capacity + food storage) / (number of passenger* number of pools)
